evidence: The hunk builds `seen = f"{SINGLETON_LOCK} -> {target}"` from the raw readlink target, and the module's own _printable docstring says foreign text is sanitised there. The agent wrapped target and checked host's !r arm, but it did not sweep the bare `pid {pid}` interpolation in the same function (F11) or the paths in the _refuse sentence (F13/F14).
guidance_note: When sanitising one foreign value in a message, list every interpolation in every sentence that value reaches and close them all in the same commit.

evidence: _plan's SeedPath arm passes `path` as its own singleton root, and _parse_seed_path accepts a profile subdirectory, so a lock one level up is missed. The ancestor walk is a sound generalisation. But walking to `/` sent every ancestor through singleton_holder's 'any OSError is held' arm, and that produced F8/F9.
guidance_note: When widening the set of inputs a predicate is called on (one dir to every ancestor), re-read that predicate's error arms against the new inputs before pushing.

evidence: '²'.isdigit() is True and int('²') raises ValueError; the agent reproduced both this and the OverflowError. Replacing isdigit with int() inside _pid_alive also widened what reaches the final arm: int() strips whitespace like \x0b, which isdigit had rejected, so a raw `pid {pid}` became an injection site (F11).
guidance_note: When swapping one parser for a more permissive one, check every downstream use of the raw text the old predicate used to gate.

evidence: The refusal said `seed = fresh`, which tomllib rejects; the agent confirmed this and quoted it. The defect is invalid TOML in a user instruction, not two sources of truth for one fact, so the law token is decoration.
guidance_note: Paste every config snippet a user-facing message suggests through the real parser in a test.

evidence: _plan's SeedChrome arm passes `root`, not `root / which`, so the README's 'the profile you are copying from' understated the scope. The fix in 398c5cc rewords it to the whole user-data-dir and adds the chrome:Work example.
guidance_note: Write README scope claims from the code path's actual argument, not from the user-level intent.

evidence: Duplicate of F3's overflow half; the agent confirmed `os.kill(10**30, 0)` raises OverflowError and fixed both in cb7d31c.

The README promised 'a browser opened halfway through is caught too', while _undisturbed documents the start-and-exit gap. 398c5cc reworded the README only and left the identical 'never reports success' overclaim in seed.py's module docstring, which F2 already quoted at seed.py:8-10 in round 0. That missed copy is F15.
guidance_note: When fixing an overclaim, grep the repo for the same promise in other docstrings and docs before committing.

evidence: The flag names 398c5cc (a README-only commit), but the real cause is F2's ancestor walk (d0ca725): every ancestor now hits singleton_holder's catch-all OSError, which reads as held, so EACCES on an unrelated ancestor refuses with a browser message. The agent's EACCES-is-free reasoning is sound, but its fac0628 os.stat rewrite narrowed the not-present arm (F16) and created an unsanitised 'cannot be read' sink (F17).
guidance_note: When widening a predicate's input set, enumerate its error arms against the new inputs; when replacing is_dir with os.stat, carry over pathlib's ignored-errno set explicitly.

evidence: Same defect as F8 on the same line, caused by F2's walk to `/`. It got the same fix (PermissionError joins the free arm) and the same rejection of the distinct 'could not check' variant, justified by the claim that EACCES on any walked path implies copytree fails.
guidance_note: Re-read every error arm of a callee whenever a fix changes which inputs reach it.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 398c5cc is README-only, and the PermissionError arm of _pid_alive predates review (F6's text says the original caught ProcessLookupError/PermissionError). The agent added the mock test and said honestly that it passes on both old and new code.
guidance_note: When a function distinguishes N outcomes of a syscall, write one test per outcome in the original PR.

evidence: The reviewer's \x1c example is wrong: the agent verified int('\x1c1\x1c') raises. But \x0b1 parses to 1, and that only reaches the `pid {pid}` line because F3's fix replaced the isdigit gate with int(). F1's fix also missed this sink. Deleting the duplicate interpolation instead of sanitising it is the better cure.
guidance_note: When loosening a parse gate, trace each raw substring the gate used to protect to every sink it reaches.

evidence: The comment written in 32eb2e4 justified EACCES-is-free with 'every path this walks is built from components of the seed's own path', which is caller knowledge inside singleton_holder. The reviewer's first remedy (EACCES back to held) would have reopened F8, so taking the docstring-only remedy was right.
guidance_note: Justify a function's behaviour in its own comment using only facts true at its own altitude, never facts about how today's caller uses it.

evidence: F1's fix sanitised only the lock target, while _refuse's sentence also interpolated raw paths: `held` (an attacker-nameable ancestor after F2's walk) and copy.described. Wrapping the whole assembled message closes both. The agent then wrongly told the reviewer _copy's messages all predate the PR; 'cannot be read' was new (F17).
guidance_note: When a fix sanitises one foreign value, sanitise the whole sentence it lands in at the assembly point, in the same commit.

evidence: This is F13 reached through the directory name rather than a planted symlink, in the same _refuse f-string F1's fix left unswept. Closed by the same 080e6a0 wrap of the assembled message.
guidance_note: Sanitise at the message-assembly point, not per value, so sibling interpolations cannot be missed.

evidence: F2's round-0 text already quotes the seed.py:8-10 'never reports success over a profile taken from under a live browser' guarantee. So 398c5cc fixed the README copy and missed this one; the agent's 'reintroduced by this round' account is wrong, but the reword is right.
guidance_note: When rewording an overclaimed guarantee, grep for the same promise across docstrings and docs and fix every copy in one commit.

evidence: fac0628 swapped Path.is_dir (which ignores ENOENT/ENOTDIR/EBADF/ELOOP) for os.stat with only FileNotFoundError as absent, so a path through a regular file became 'cannot be read'; the agent confirmed this. Leaving ELOOP in 'cannot be read' is a defended choice.
guidance_note: When replacing a library predicate with a lower-level call, write down the errors the predicate absorbed and map each one explicitly.

evidence: The 'cannot be read' sink was created by F8's fac0628 (the agent confirmed it is absent on master). F13's fix wrapped _refuse but left this sibling raw, wrongly calling it pre-existing. The reviewer's ELOOP reachability example is wrong (singleton_holder refuses ELOOP first, as the agent showed), but EACCES reaches the sink.
guidance_note: When sweeping a class of unsanitised messages, check each sink against master before classifying it as pre-existing.

evidence: The flag is a false positive for causation: the agent shows the raw 'does not exist' interpolation is on master at seed.py:122, and c551bab only added NotADirectoryError to the arm above it. It was fixed for consistency with the adjacent new wrap, and the class stays ticketed.

This is a pre-existing gap, not caused by c336284. On master, is_dir's stat also succeeds on a chmod-000 dir with normal parents and falls through to the same uncaught copytree. The agent reproduced it, filed crom-seeding-9o5 with the repro and the two copytree failure shapes, and deferred it out of the PR.

The flag is a false positive: the paragraph introducing singleton_holder(Path) is in the module docstring hunk from the original PR, so 'Everything here takes a ResolvedProfile' was false before any fix. The agent deleted the false premise rather than enumerating exceptions.
guidance_note: When adding a paragraph that carves an exception into a module docstring, re-read the adjacent universal claims in the same edit.

narrative: Round 0 raised seven real defects in the original PR, and every one was correctly accepted, mostly with well-reasoned broader fixes. Those fixes then produced most of the later findings. The ancestor walk (F2) pushed EACCES on unrelated ancestors into the held arm (F8/F9), and the EACCES fix's os.stat rewrite narrowed absent-detection (F16) and created a new unsanitised sink (F17). Replacing isdigit with int() opened a \x0b injection through the raw pid (F11). Sanitising only the lock target (F1) and fixing only the README overclaim (F7) left sibling instances (F13/F14, F15). Round 4's findings were pre-existing or original-PR drift, and round 5 hit the review cap, so the final commit went unreviewed.
guidance_observations: Fixes repeatedly widened a callee's input set or swapped a predicate without re-auditing the callee's error arms and downstream sinks, so each round's fix seeded the next round's findings.
Sanitisation was applied value by value through three rounds before landing at the message-assembly point; doing that on the first injection finding would have removed F13, F14 and F17.
The agent once classified a sink as pre-existing without checking master, and the reviewer had to flag it the next round; checking master before ticketing a deferral would have prevented that.
The flagged commits (398c5cc, d3d7d44, c551bab, c336284) were usually not the true cause; the anchoring commit and the causal fix commit differed in most rounds.

evidence: `raise CromError(f"{problem}{_stop_after_failure(profile)}")` evaluates find_pids, and through it scan(), inside the f-string, so a ps failure replaces the launch diagnosis. The agent traced the full call chain and widened the catch to OSError for os.kill's PermissionError, with a test showing the OSError half is load-bearing.
guidance_note: When adding cleanup inside an error-construction expression, make the cleanup total (catch and fold its failures into text) before wiring it in.

evidence: The reviewer's reason is wrong: _Exited/_NeverAnswered are reachable only while the port probe returns _Silent, so the port never answered. But a Chrome that bound the socket without serving /json/version still holds it, so waiting on _still_held for the blind arms is right. The agent corrected the rationale and applied the per-arm demand.
guidance_note: When choosing a cleanup demand for several failure arms, derive it per arm from what each arm's evidence proves about resource ownership.

narrative: One review round found two real defects introduced by the PR's own refactor: cleanup inside the error f-string could replace the launch diagnosis, and a processes-only demand skipped the agent's own port teardown. Both were fixed in one commit with tests confirmed to fail on revert, and round 1 approved with no new findings. No finding came from a fix.
guidance_observations: The agent corrected a wrong reviewer rationale while still accepting the cure, which kept the docstring's reasoning accurate instead of inheriting the reviewer's false premise.
